title: For Such a Time as This
subtitle: Esther in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Esther begins with a banquet that lasts half a year and ends with neighbors carrying plates of food to one another's doors. In between: an orphan girl raised by her cousin, a jar of myrrh, a man who will not bow, a lot cast for a day of ruin, three days of fasting, a golden scepter held out, a king who cannot sleep, and a book of records opened to exactly the right page.

This book walks through it in thirty-two short poems, in four parts. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The name of God is never written in the book of Esther, and the poems try to notice where his hand is hidden anyway. The pictures stay with the things the story touches—a signet ring, a sleepless lamp, a table set for three —and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the book of Esther alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: one hundred eighty days
paintings.epigraph: “He displayed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honor of his excellent majesty many days”
paintings.poem:
half a year
of showing off.

white and blue hangings,
silver rings,
couches of gold
on a floor of colored stone,
wine poured
from cups no two alike.

every name in the empire
was spoken in that garden
except one.

the story never says it.
keep reading anyway.
he is there.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“half a year of showing off”) and the closing thought (“keep reading anyway. he is there”), what is Esther 1:4–7 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
半年
炫耀。

白色和蓝色的帷幔，
银戒指，
黄金沙发
在彩色石头的地板上，
倒酒
从杯子来看，没有两个是一样的。

帝国中的每一个名字
在那个花园里有人说过
除了一个。

故事从来没有说过。
无论如何，继续阅读。
他在那儿。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“半年的炫耀”）和结束语（“无论如何，继续读下去。他就在那里”）之间，以斯帖记 1:4-7 在你那个时代温和地重构了什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “许多天他展示了他光荣王国的财富和他卓越陛下的荣耀”

paintings.title: the queen who would not come
paintings.epigraph: “But the queen V ashti refused to come at the king’s commandment”
paintings.poem:
seven days of wine,
and the king sent for her
to be looked at.

she said no.

the whole empire
wrote a law about it,
and she walks out
of the story
without another word.

but a door
has been left open
in the palace,

and someone
no one has heard of yet
is on her way.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of For Such a Time as This, “the queen who would not come” (Esther 1:10–12) slows us down at the open threshold to remind us: “but a door has been left open in the palace, and someone no one has heard of yet is on her way.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
七日酒，
国王派人去接她
待观察。

她说不。

整个帝国
制定了相关法律，
她走出去
故事的
无需多言。

但有一扇门
已打开
在宫殿里，

和某人
还没人听说过
正在路上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《今生今世》的路上，“不肯来的王后”（以斯帖记 1：10-12）在敞开的门槛处放慢了我们的速度，提醒我们：“但王宫里的一扇门一直开着，有一个还没有人听说过的人正在赶来的路上。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但王后瓦阿什提拒绝遵照国王的命令前来”

paintings.title: myrtle
paintings.epigraph: “for she had neither father nor mother.”
paintings.poem:
no father.
no mother.
a long way from Jerusalem.

just a cousin
who took her in
and called her daughter.

she had two names,
one for the empire
and one for home.

God is like that
in this book too:
unnamed,
and caring for her
all the same.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “myrtle” (Esther 2:5–7), what would you talk about after reading, “God is like that in this book too: unnamed, and caring for her all the same”?
paintings.zh_poem:
没有父亲。
没有母亲。
距离耶路撒冷很远。

只是一个表弟
谁收留了她
并打电话给她的女儿。

她有两个名字，
为帝国而生的一员
以及一份家用。

神就是这样的
也在这本书中：
无名，
并照顾她
都一样。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，停在“桃金娘”处（以斯帖记 2:5-7），当你读到“神在这本书里也是如此，没有名字，却照样关心她”之后，你会谈论什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为她既没有父亲，也没有母亲。”

paintings.title: every day by the court
paintings.epigraph: “Mordecai walked every day in front of the court of the women’s house, to find out how Esther was doing”
paintings.poem:
he couldn't go in.
he could only walk past.

every day
the same wall,
the same gate,
the same question:
how is she?

some love
can only stand outside
and ask.

it still counts.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the stones of the wall: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “every day by the court”—“some love can only stand outside and ask. it still counts”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他不能进去。
他只能走过去。

每天
同一面墙，
同一个门，
同样的问题：
她怎么样？

一些爱
只能站在外面
并询问。

它仍然很重要。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 驻足在墙石前：今天，当你坐在《天天朝庭旁》的结语——“有些爱只能站在外面问，还是算数”时，你的姿势有什么变化？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “末底改每天都在女院门前行走，看看以斯帖过得怎么样”

paintings.title: twelve months of myrrh
paintings.epigraph: “six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet fragrances”
paintings.poem:
a whole year
of oil and perfume
before one evening
with the king.

she was being made ready
for a crown.

she didn't know
she was also being made ready
for a day
when she would have to
walk in uninvited.

the long waiting
is never
only waiting.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the weight of the crown in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “the long waiting is never only waiting” (Esther 2:12)?
paintings.zh_poem:
整整一年
油和香水
一天晚上之前
与国王。

她正在做好准备
为了一顶王冠。

她不知道
她也正在做好准备
一天
当她不得不
不请自来地走进来。

漫长的等待
从来没有
只能等待。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画中王冠重量的静止：当你思考“长久的等待，绝不仅仅是等待”（以斯帖记 2:12）时，你还能放下什么努力呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “六个月没药油，六个月甜香”

paintings.title: she required nothing
paintings.epigraph: “she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s eunuch, the keeper of the women, advised.”
paintings.poem:
she could have asked
for anything to take with her:
jewels, silk, gold.

she asked for nothing
but good advice.

and the girl
who reached for nothing
was handed a crown.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Esther 2:15–17, the story turns on the weight of the crown—and ends with, “and the girl who reached for nothing was handed a crown.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
她本可以问
随身携带的物品：
珠宝、丝绸、黄金。

她什么也没要求
但很好的建议。

和那个女孩
谁一无所获
被授予一顶王冠。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在以斯帖记 2 章 15-17 节中，故事的重点是王冠的重量，并以“那无所求的女孩得到了王冠”作为结尾。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “她只需要国王的太监、妇女的守护者希该的建议。”

paintings.title: written in the book
paintings.epigraph: “it was written in the book of the chronicles in the king’s presence.”
paintings.poem:
a whisper at the gate.
a plot against the king.
Mordecai heard it
and told.

the matter was settled,
a scribe wrote it down,
and the scroll went on a shelf.

no reward.
no thank you.

just a line
in a book no one reads.

hold on to that line.
it will be read aloud
on exactly the right night.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Esther 2:21–23 points us to the city gate and whispers, “it will be read aloud on exactly the right night.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
门口传来一阵窃窃私语。
反对国王的阴谋
末底改听见了
并告诉。

事情已经解决了，
一位抄写员把它写下来，
卷轴被放在架子上。

没有奖励。
不，谢谢。

只是一条线
在一本没有人读的书中。

坚持住那条线。
它将被大声朗读
在正确的夜晚。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界以速度和噪音来衡量生命，但《以斯帖记》2:21-23 却把我们引向城门，低声说道：“在正确的夜晚，人们会大声朗读它。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这是在国王面前写在编年史上的。”

paintings.title: he would not bow
paintings.epigraph: “But Mordecai didn’t bow down or pay him homage.”
paintings.poem:
everyone at the gate
bent low
when Haman walked by.

one man
stayed standing.

they asked him why,
day after day.

his answer
was only this:
i am a Jew.

some knees
are already
spoken for.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “some knees are already spoken for.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
每个人都在门口
低弯
当哈曼走过时。

一个人
一直站着。

他们问他为什么，
日复一日。

他的回答
只是这样：
我是犹太人。

一些膝盖
已经
为之发言。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“有些膝盖已经被提及了。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但末底改并没有跪拜或向他致敬。”

paintings.title: the lot
paintings.epigraph: “they cast Pur, that is, the lot”
paintings.poem:
Haman let chance
choose the day.

day after day
the lots rolled,
month after month,

until they stopped
on the twelfth month,
almost a year away.

he thought
he was picking a date.

he was giving
the other side
almost a year.

another book says
the lot is cast into the lap,
but the answer
comes from the Lord.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “another book says the lot is cast into the lap, but the answer comes from the Lord” (Esther 3:7) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
哈曼让机会
选择日子。

日复一日
批次滚动，
月复一月，

直到他们停下来
第十二个月，
快一年了。

他想
他正在挑选一个日期。

他正在给予
另一边
快一年了。

另一本书说
地块被抛在膝上，
但答案
来自主。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时候，一句话可以在封闭的房间里打开一扇窗：“又有一本书说，签放在怀里，但应允从耶和华而来”（以斯帖记 3:7）如何解答你最近一直困扰的一个问题？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们投了 Pur，也就是抽签”

paintings.title: the ring
paintings.epigraph: “The king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman”
paintings.poem:
a ring slid off one finger
and onto another.

that was all it took.

no one asked
who the people were
or what they had done.

a signet ring
has no conscience.
it only presses
what it's told.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “the ring” (Esther 3:10–11): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “it only presses what it's told”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一枚戒指从一根手指上滑落
然后到另一个。

就这样了。

没有人问
这些人是谁
或者他们做了什么。

一枚图章戒指
没有良心。
它只按
它讲述了什么。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“指环”之前张开双手（以斯帖记 3：10-11）：当你听到“它只按所吩咐的”时，你紧握的是什么东西就松开了？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “国王从他手上取下戒指，交给哈曼”

paintings.title: the city was perplexed
paintings.epigraph: “The king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Susa was perplexed.”
paintings.poem:
in the palace,
two men raised their cups.

in the streets,
a whole city
stood reading the notice
and could not make sense of it.

the powerful
are often
the last to notice
what they have done.

the city
knew something was wrong.

so did heaven.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Esther 3:15 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “the city knew something was wrong. so did heaven” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
在宫殿里，
两个人举起了杯子。

在街道上，
整个城市
站着读通知
并且无法理解它。

有权有势的人
经常
最后注意到的
他们做了什么。

城市
知道出了什么问题。

天堂也是如此。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经在以斯帖记 3 章 15 节中记住这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻印象，而是为了让我们坚定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到过“城知道出了问题，天也知道出了问题”的真理？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “王与哈曼坐下喝酒；书珊城的人却都困惑不解。”

paintings.title: sackcloth
paintings.epigraph: “Mordecai tore his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes”
paintings.poem:
he tore his clothes
and walked into the middle of the city
and cried out loud.

they don't let sackcloth
through the king's gate.

but grief
has other doors.

in every province
where the letter came,
people lay down in ashes
and did not eat.

the book does not say
who they were crying to.

it doesn't have to.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “sackcloth” (Esther 4:1–3), what one honest sentence would you pray beside the open threshold after reading, “the book does not say who they were crying to. it doesn't have to”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他撕破了衣服
走进城市的中心
并大声喊叫。

他们不让麻布
通过国王的大门。

但悲伤
还有其他门。

在每个省份
信来的地方，
人们躺在灰烬中
并没有吃饭。

书上没有说
他们向谁哭泣。

没必要。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼停在“麻布”处时（以斯帖记 4：1-3），读完“书上没有说他们向谁哭泣。不必如此”之后，你会在敞开的门槛旁祈祷哪一句诚实的句子？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “末底改撕裂衣服，穿上撒满灰的麻布”

paintings.title: thirty days
paintings.epigraph: “I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”
paintings.poem:
queen,
and still afraid
of a door.

thirty days
without a word from him.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“queen, and still afraid of a door”) and the closing thought (“thirty days without a word from him”), what is Esther 4:11 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
女王,
并且仍然害怕
一扇门的。

三十天
他一言不发。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“王后，仍然害怕一扇门”）和结束语（“三十天没有他的消息”）之间，以斯帖记 4:11 在你那个时代温柔地重构了什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这三十天了，我没有被叫去见国王。”

paintings.title: from another place
paintings.epigraph: “relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place”
paintings.poem:
if you stay quiet,
Mordecai said,
help will still come.
from another place.

he didn't say
whose place.

he didn't need to.

the rescue
was never
riding on her.

the question was only
whether she would
be part of it.

who knows?
maybe this is why
you are where you are.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of For Such a Time as This, “from another place” (Esther 4:13–14) slows us down at the quiet centerpiece of “from another place” to remind us: “maybe this is why you are where you are.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
如果你保持安静
末底改说，
帮助仍然会来。
从另一个地方。

他没有说
谁的位置。

他不需要。

救援
从来没有
骑在她身上。

问题只是
她是否会
成为其中的一部分。

谁知道？
也许这就是为什么
你就在你所在的地方。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 沿着《今生今世》的道路，“从别处来”（以斯帖记 4：13-14）让我们在“从别处来”的安静中心放慢脚步，提醒我们：“也许这就是你现在所在的原因。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “犹太人将从另一个地方得到解脱和拯救”

paintings.title: the fast
paintings.epigraph: “fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day.”
paintings.poem:
before the queen
went in to the king,
a whole city
went without bread.

three days.
three nights.
no food, no water.

and the maidens in the palace
did the same.

nobody wrote down the prayers.

but an empty bowl
is a kind of prayer,

and so many empty bowls
across one city
make a sound
heaven can hear.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “the fast” (Esther 4:16), what would you talk about after reading, “but an empty bowl is a kind of prayer, and so many empty bowls across one city make a sound heaven can hear”?
paintings.zh_poem:
在女王面前
进到国王那里去，
整个城市
没有面包。

三天。
三个晚上。
没有食物，没有水。

还有宫里的宫女们
也做了同样的事。

没有人写下祈祷文。

但一个空碗
是一种祈祷，

还有那么多空碗
跨越一座城市
发出声音
天能听见。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，并在“禁食”处停下来（以斯帖记 4:16），当你读到“但空碗也是一种祷告，而一座城里有那么多空碗发出天上能听见的声音”之后，你会谈论什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “为我禁食，三天三夜，不吃不喝。”

paintings.title: if I perish
paintings.epigraph: “if I perish, I perish.”
paintings.poem:
she did not say
i will not perish.

she said
i am going in.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the quiet centerpiece of “if I perish”: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “if I perish”—“she said i am going in”?
paintings.zh_poem:
她没有说
我不会灭亡。

她说
我要进去了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“如果我灭亡”的安静中心部分前停顿一下：今天，当你坐在“如果我灭亡”的结束语——“她说我要进去”时，你的姿势有什么变化？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “如果我死了，我就死了。”

paintings.title: the third day
paintings.epigraph: “Now on the third day, Esther put on her royal clothing”
paintings.poem:
on the third day
she put the robe back on.

three days hungry.
three days praying.
and now the purple
and the crown.

she did not walk in
as a beggar.

she walked in
as who she was,

and let the fasting
be the part
no one could see.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the weight of the crown in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “she walked in as who she was, and let the fasting be the part no one could see” (Esther 5:1)?
paintings.zh_poem:
第三天
她重新穿上长袍。

饿了三天。
三天祈祷。
现在是紫色
和王冠。

她没有走进去
作为一个乞丐。

她走进来
正如她是谁，

并让禁食
成为其中的一部分
没有人能看到。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画中王冠重量的静止：当你沉思“她按着自己的身份走进去，禁食成为无人能见的部分”（以斯帖记 5:1）时，你能放下什么努力呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “第三天，以斯帖穿上她的王服”

paintings.title: the golden scepter
paintings.epigraph: “the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand.”
paintings.poem:
the law said
one of two things
would happen.

she stood in the court
and waited
to find out which.

and the king
held out the gold.

she came near
and touched the tip.

that is all.
a hand stretched out,
and another hand
reaching back.

you can build
a whole faith
on a moment like that.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Esther 5:2, the story turns on the extended golden scepter—and ends with, “you can build a whole faith on a moment like that.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
法律说
两件事之一
会发生的。

她站在法庭上
并等待
找出哪个。

和国王
拿出了金子。

她走近了
并触摸了尖端。

仅此而已。
伸出一只手，
和另一只手
回来。

你可以建造
整个信仰
在那样的时刻。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在以斯帖记 5 章 2 节中，故事以伸出的金权杖为中心，并以“你可以在这样的时刻建立完整的信仰”结束。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “国王向以斯帖伸出了手中的金权杖。”

paintings.title: a table for three
paintings.epigraph: “let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”
paintings.poem:
up to half the kingdom,
he said.

she asked for dinner.

and at dinner,
asked for dinner again.

she was not afraid
to be slow.

some things
are not rushed
into the open.

they are served
in their time.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Esther 5:4 points us to the table set before you and whispers, “they are served in their time.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
多达半个王国，
他说。

她要吃晚饭。

晚餐时，
再次要求吃饭。

她不害怕
慢一点。

有些事情
不着急
进入公开状态。

他们得到服务
在他们的时代。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界以速度和噪音来衡量生命，但以斯帖记 5:4 却向我们指出摆在你面前的桌子，低声说道：“他们得着各时的服务。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “今天请王和哈曼来参加我为他准备的宴会。”

paintings.title: all this avails me nothing
paintings.epigraph: “Y et all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”
paintings.poem:
riches.
sons.
promotions.
dinner with the queen.

he counted every one
out loud.

and then said
none of it mattered
because one man
would not stand up.

a heart like that
could own the whole empire
and still be hungry.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “a heart like that could own the whole empire and still be hungry.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
财富。
儿子们。
促销活动。
与女王共进晚餐。

他数了每一个
大声说出来。

然后说
一切都不重要
因为一个人
不会站起来。

一颗这样的心
可以拥有整个帝国
而且还是很饿。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“一颗这样的心可以拥有整个帝国，但仍然会感到饥饿。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “然而，只要我看到犹太人末底改坐在王门前，这一切就对我没有任何帮助。”

paintings.title: the sleepless king
paintings.epigraph: “He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.”
paintings.poem:
that night
the most powerful man in the world
could not sleep.

nothing unusual.
kings lie awake.

so he did
what tired men do
and asked for something dull
to be read to him.

the story doesn't say
who kept him up.

it just leaves
the lamp on.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “it just leaves the lamp on” (Esther 6:1) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
那天晚上
世界上最有权势的人
睡不着。

没什么不寻常的。
国王们醒着。

所以他做到了
疲惫的男人会做什么
并要求一些无聊的东西
读给他听。

故事没有说
谁让他坚持下去的。

它只是离开
灯亮了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时候，一句话就能在封闭的房间里打开一扇窗：“它只是让灯亮着”（以斯帖记 6:1）如何解答你最近一直在思考的一个问题？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他命人将编年史的记录书带来，并向国王宣读。”

paintings.title: nothing has been done
paintings.epigraph: ““Nothing has been done for him.””
paintings.poem:
out of all those scrolls,
all those years,
the reader stopped
on one line:

Mordecai.
the plot at the gate.

and the king asked,
what did we do for him?

nothing.

good done in secret
can sit on a shelf
a long time.

it is not lost.
it is waiting
for the right night.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “nothing has been done” (Esther 6:2–3): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “it is waiting for the right night”?
paintings.zh_poem:
从所有这些卷轴中，
那些年，
读者停了下来
一行：

末底改。
门口的情节。

国王问道：
我们为他做了什么？

没有什么。

秘密做的好事
可以放在架子上
很长一段时间。

它并没有丢失。
它正在等待
为正确的夜晚。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“什么都没有发生”之前（以斯帖记 6：2-3），请张开双手：当你听到“等待正确的夜晚”时，你紧握的是什么松开了？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我们没有为他做任何事。”

paintings.title: the man the king delights to honor
paintings.epigraph: “Thus it shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”
paintings.poem:
who could the king
want to honor
more than me?
Haman thought.

so he described
the robe,
the horse,
the crown,
the parade.

and then was told
to lead the horse himself
and call out the words

for Mordecai.

he walked home
with his head covered.

the one who had stayed standing
rode.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Esther 6:6–11 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “the one who had stayed standing rode” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
谁能成为国王
想要荣誉
比我还多？
哈曼心想。

所以他描述了
长袍，
马，
皇冠,
游行。

然后被告知
亲自牵马
并喊出这些话

为了末底改。

他步行回家
蒙着头。

那个一直站着的人
骑了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经在以斯帖记 6:6-11 中记住这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻印象，而是为了让我们稳定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到过“那站着的人骑马了”的真理？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “凡是国王所喜悦尊崇的人，都将如此！”

paintings.title: my people
paintings.epigraph: “let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.”
paintings.poem:
the second banquet.
the same question.
what do you want?

this time she said it:
my life,
and my people.

for years
she had kept quiet
about who she was.

now she said it
in front of the man
who wanted them gone.

hiding had kept her safe.
telling the truth
kept them alive.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “my people” (Esther 7:3–4), what one honest sentence would you pray beside the quiet centerpiece of “my people” after reading, “telling the truth kept them alive”?
paintings.zh_poem:
第二次宴会。
同样的问题。
你想要什么？

这次她说：
我的生活，
和我的人民。

多年来
她一直保持沉默
关于她是谁。

现在她说了
在男人面前
谁想要他们离开。

躲藏保证了她的安全。
说实话
让他们活下去。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼停在“我的百姓”（以斯帖记 7：3-4）处时，读完“说真话使他们活下去”之后，你会在“我的百姓”安静的核心内容旁边祈祷哪一句诚实的句子？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “应我的请求，赐予我生命；应我的请求，赐予我的人民。”

paintings.title: the one he built
paintings.epigraph: “Then the king’s wrath was pacified.”
paintings.poem:
the thing Haman had built
for Mordecai
was the thing
that ended him.

the story says it
in one short line
and doesn't stay to watch.

neither will we.

a pit dug for someone else
has a way
of keeping its digger.

and the king's anger
went quiet.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“the thing Haman had built for Mordecai was the thing that ended him”) and the closing thought (“and the king's anger went quiet”), what is Esther 7:9–10 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
哈曼建造的东西
为了末底改
就是这样
那结束了他。

故事说的是
短短一行
并且不会留下来观看。

我们也不会。

给别人挖的坑
有办法
保留其挖掘机。

和国王的愤怒
安静了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“哈曼为末底改建造的东西却终结了他”）和结束语（“王的怒气就平息了”）之间，《以斯帖记》7:9-10 在你那个时代温和地重构了什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这样，国王的愤怒就平息了。”

paintings.title: the ring again
paintings.epigraph: “The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai.”
paintings.poem:
the same ring.
the same king.

a few chapters ago
it sealed a death sentence.

now it rests
on the hand
of the man
it was meant to erase.

the old seal
could not be broken.

so a new one
was pressed
beside it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of For Such a Time as This, “the ring again” (Esther 8:2) slows us down at your own two hands to remind us: “so a new one was pressed beside it.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
同一个戒指。
同一个国王。

几章前
它宣告了死刑。

现在它休息了
在手上
那个男人的
它是为了擦除。

旧印章
无法被打破。

所以一个新的
被压
在它旁边。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《为这样的时刻》的道路上，“戒指又响了”（以斯帖记 8:2），你的两只手使我们放慢了速度，提醒我们：“所以旁边又压了一个新的戒指。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “王摘下从哈曼那里夺来的戒指，交给末底改。”

paintings.title: how can I endure
paintings.epigraph: “For how can I endure to see the evil that would come to my people?”
paintings.poem:
Haman was gone,
and she had a house,
and she was safe.

it would have been easy
to stop there.

she fell down
at the king's feet again
and wept.

she could not
be happy alone.

and the scepter
came out a second time.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “how can I endure” (Esther 8:3–6), what would you talk about after reading, “and the scepter came out a second time”?
paintings.zh_poem:
哈曼走了，
而且她有一所房子，
她很安全。

本来很容易
停在那里。

她摔倒了
再次拜倒在国王脚下
并哭了。

她不能
一个人也要快乐。

和权杖
第二次出来了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，并停在“我怎能忍耐”（以斯帖记 8：3-6），那么在读到“权杖第二次出来”之后，你会谈论什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我怎么能忍受看到我的人民遭受不幸呢？”

paintings.title: swift horses
paintings.epigraph: “sent letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that were bred from swift steeds.”
paintings.poem:
the first letter
could not be taken back.
Persian law.

so a second letter
went out after it,
faster,
on the king's best horses,

every province,
every language,
every road:

you may stand
and defend your lives.

the first word
was still written.

it just wasn't
the last word anymore.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the quiet centerpiece of “swift horses”: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “swift horses”—“it just wasn't the last word anymore”?
paintings.zh_poem:
第一个字母
无法收回。
波斯法。

所以第二个字母
之后就出去了，
更快，
骑着国王最好的马，

每个省，
每种语言，
每条路：

你可以站着
并保卫你的生命。

第一个词
仍然写着。

它只是不是
最后一句话再说了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在安静的核心“千里马”前停顿一下：今天，当你坐在“千里马”的结束语——“这不再是最后一个词”时，你的姿势有什么变化？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “信使骑马寄信，骑着由快马培育出来的皇家马匹。”

paintings.title: light and gladness
paintings.epigraph: “The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor.”
paintings.poem:
Mordecai walked out
in blue and white
and a crown of gold.

the city that had been perplexed
started shouting.

light,
gladness,
joy,
honor.

four words
where there had been
ashes.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the weight of the crown in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “four words where there had been ashes” (Esther 8:15–17)?
paintings.zh_poem:
末底改走了出去
蓝色和白色
和一顶金冠。

这座曾经困惑的城市
开始大喊大叫。

光，
高兴，
喜悦，
荣誉。

四个字
曾经有过的地方
灰烬。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画中王冠重量的静止：当你沉思“已成灰的四个字”（以斯帖记 8：15-17）时，你能放下什么努力呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “犹太人有光明、喜乐、喜乐和荣耀。”

paintings.title: the other way
paintings.epigraph: “but it was turned out the opposite happened”
paintings.poem:
the day that was chosen
to end them
came.

and it turned
the other way.

they stood together
and were not destroyed.
and the book notes
they left the plunder where it lay.

you can look at the back
of a weaving
and see only knots.

this book lets us
turn it over.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Esther 9:1, the story turns on the quiet centerpiece of “the other way”—and ends with, “this book lets us turn it over.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
选定的日子
结束他们
来了。

然后它变成了
另一种方式。

他们站在一起
并且没有被摧毁。
和书上的笔记
他们把战利品留在原地。

你可以看看后面
一个编织的
并且只看到结。

这本书让我们
把它翻过来。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在以斯帖记 9 章 1 节中，故事转向了“另一条路”的安静核心，并以“这本书让我们把它翻过来”结束。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但事实证明相反的情况发生了”

paintings.title: portions
paintings.epigraph: “sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.”
paintings.poem:
how do you remember
being rescued?

Mordecai wrote it down:

feast.
be glad.
carry plates of food
to your neighbor's door.

and don't forget
the ones with nothing.

a people once sold
now give things away.

that is how
you know
the sorrow
has really turned.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Esther 9:19–22 points us to the open threshold and whispers, “that is how you know the sorrow has really turned.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
你怎么记得
被救了？

末底改写下它：

盛宴。
高兴吧。
端着盘子里的食物
到你邻居家门口。

别忘了
那些一无所有的人。

一个曾经被卖掉的人
现在把东西放弃。

就是这样
你知道
悲伤
真的变了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界以速度和噪音来衡量生命，但以斯帖记 9:19-22 却向我们指出了敞开的门槛，并轻声说道：“这就是你知道悲伤真正转变的方式。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “互相赠送食物，并向有需要的人赠送礼物。”

paintings.title: Purim
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore they called these days “Purim”, from the word “Pur.””
paintings.poem:
they named the feast
after the lot
rolled to choose
the day of their ending.

a strange name
for a celebration,
unless the point is:
they are still here.

his name
is never written in this book.

but every year
they tell the story again,

and every year
someone notices
whose hand
was underneath.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “but every year they tell the story again, and every year someone notices whose hand was underneath.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
他们把这个节日命名为
拍完后
滚动选择
他们结束的那一天。

一个奇怪的名字
为了庆祝，
除非要点是：
他们还在这里。

他的名字
本书中从未写过。

但每年
他们再次讲述这个故事，

并且每年
有人注意到
谁的手
在下面。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以安静的转折结束：“但每年他们都会再次讲述这个故事，每年都会有人注意到谁的手在下面。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因此，他们称这些日子为‘普珥节’，源自‘Pur’这个词。”

zh_beforeYouBegin:
以斯帖以一场持续半年的宴会开始，以邻居们端着盘子的食物到彼此家门口结束。其间：一个由表弟养大的孤女，一罐没药，一个不肯鞠躬的男人，为一日毁灭而抽签，三天斋戒，一根金权杖，一个无法入睡的国王，以及一本翻到正确页码的记录簿。

本书分为四部分，用三十二首短诗来讲述它。每首诗都位于一幅画旁边和一行经文之下。以斯帖记中从未写过上帝的名字，而这些诗却试图注意到他的手藏在哪里。这些图片与故事所涉及的事物并存——一枚图章戒指、一盏不眠灯、一张三人桌——并将面孔留给你想象。

这些诗不是圣经。它们是一位读者对此的回应。打开这本书旁边的以斯帖记，让真实的话语成为最后的话语。
